assignment.acceptance_condition: A structured report covering (a)-(d) with effect directions and statistics and explicit PDF page markers from papers/text/lorenz-et-al-2011-social-influence.txt.
assignment.objective: What does Lorenz et al. 2011 'How Social Influence Can Undermine the Wisdom of Crowd Effect' establish? Extract: (a) experimental design (estimation tasks, subjects, information conditions: no information, aggregate information, full information); (b) the quantified effects of social influence on accuracy, on diversity/range reduction, and on confidence, with numbers; (c) the mechanism by which social influence narrows diversity without improving collective accuracy; (d) conditions under which influence helped versus hurt. Record every claim with its explicit ===== PDF PAGE N ===== marker.
assignment.rationale: This is the causal-mechanism keystone for the 'open shared transcript destroys diversity' pathway in the D3 causal model; it is human evidence, so it must be flagged as cross-domain inference when applied to LLM agents.

available_experiments.description: Deterministically count lines, words, characters, and unique lexical tokens in one source material or snapshotted workspace file.
available_experiments.name: text_statistics

constraints: Use only files under papers/text as external evidence.
Citations must name the workspace file and an explicit `===== PDF PAGE N =====` marker.
Distinguish reported findings, cross-paper inference, and the note author’s new hypothesis.
Do not treat agreement, graph centrality, retrieval rank, or number of agents as evidence of truth.
Do not resolve conflicting studies by silently selecting the preferred outcome.

demands.rationale: The benchmark needs enough room for theory, evidence, and an executable study design.
demands.statement: Produce one coherent research note of 2,000–2,600 words.

demands.rationale: A research problem requires an explanatory claim, not a survey.
demands.statement: State one original mechanistic thesis about when staged retrieval-mediated Q/A communication wins or loses under matched inference compute.

demands.rationale: The model must expose variables and pathways that can be tested.
demands.statement: Construct an explicit causal model connecting initial error correlation, evidence diversity, social influence or conformity, retrieval selectivity, synthesis competence, and task topology.

demands.rationale: The corpus was selected to contain incompatible-looking results.
demands.statement: Use and reconcile all relevant positive, null, and adverse findings in the seven-file corpus, with citations to file paths and PDF page markers.

demands.rationale: Predictions are the bridge from explanation to falsification.
demands.statement: Derive at least four directional or interaction predictions that discriminate the proposed mechanism from compute-only, diversity-only, and deliberation-only alternatives.

demands.rationale: The note must not overclaim from heterogeneous published studies.
demands.statement: Identify non-identifiability, measurement, and external-validity limits in the existing evidence.

demands.rationale: A concrete study should be executable by another lab.
demands.statement: Specify a preregisterable matched-compute experiment: units, task strata, conditions, randomization, intervention fidelity, primary and secondary estimands, outcome measures, power-analysis inputs, exclusion rules, multiple-testing control, and failure or stopping criteria.

demands.rationale: The result must expose its epistemic boundary.
demands.statement: End with the strongest warranted conclusion, material unresolved questions, and the single observation most likely to falsify the thesis.

context.product_intent: Stress-test adaptive inquiry on a genuinely open research problem whose useful decomposition cannot be known before reading conflicting evidence. The result should contribute a falsifiable explanatory hypothesis and experiment, not an architecture recommendation or literature memo.
stable_context: The comparison is matched total inference compute, not matched number of agents or calls.
The three focal communication conditions are staged retrieval-mediated Q/A, independent sampling plus final aggregation, and an open shared transcript.
Published benchmark accuracy is not assumed to transfer across task topology; task-level moderators are part of the research question.
The seven extracted texts in papers/text are the complete evidentiary corpus for this benchmark; page markers are explicit in each file.
context.task: Write a 2,000–2,600 word research note that develops and defends a new mechanistic answer to this question: under a matched inference-compute budget, when should staged, retrieval-mediated question/answer communication among language-model agents outperform both independent sampling with final aggregation and an open shared transcript? Use the supplied seven-paper corpus as evidence, but do not merely survey it. Reconcile its conflicting empirical findings; formulate an explicit causal model of information diversity, social influence, retrieval, and synthesis; derive at least four discriminating predictions that separate your mechanism from plausible alternatives; identify what the existing literature cannot identify; and give a preregisterable experiment with conditions, randomization, estimands, power-analysis inputs, failure criteria, and an analysis plan. End with the strongest warranted conclusion and the observation most likely to falsify it.
context.title: Research problem: when does structured inter-agent communication help?
